recentItems.title: Aimpoint's 3.5x Scope for French Trials
recentItems.description:
Aimpoint is known for its red dot optics, but in the early 2000s the company decided to develop a 3.5x fixed magnification traditional scope. It was intended for a French military trial, and Aimpoint used their 3x magnifier as the base for building it. I have three different iterations of the project to show, none of which ended up winning the contract.

recentItems.title: Saco Defense M683: A Super-Simple SMG for the US Army
recentItems.description:
During the 1980s, the US ran the Joint Service Small Arms Program to reduce the number of different small arms in US inventory. The most significant outcome of this program was the M9 pistol, but the program also considered adopting a submachine gun. The requirements were bit tricky, with things like a low rate of fire but also a very high-ROF burst option, and caliber conversion options. Saco Defense got its hands on a Brazilian Uru submachine gun and used it as a model for their Model 683 for this program. Only a few were made, and we are taking a look at them today...

Thanks to the Institute of Military Technology for allowing me to have access to these prototypes and bring them to you! Check them out at:
http://www.instmiltech.com

recentItems.title: Announcing Varusteleka's US Expansion
recentItems.description:
https://www.varusteleka.com

Having been a customer of Varusteleka for more than 10 years and having become person friends with many of the folks there, I am very excited to share the news of their US expansion!  They now have a US distribution center, allowing them to ship fast and tariff-friction-free in the US.

Not familiar with Varusteleka? They make a wide array of outdoor gear for hunting, hiking, and military service, from clothing to web gear to pouches and more. From their early roots selling surplus, they brought a unique and very real style of brutal and dark Finnish humor; just the thing one would expect from a country that is mosquito plagued swamp when it's not sunless icy forests, with a looming 800+ mile border with Russia. They bring that attitude and the very real need for rugged top quality to their products. Looking flashy on Instagram works great for lots of brands, but Varusteleka makes kit that will be there for you when the sun disappears, the fire dies, and you fall through the ice.

recentItems.title: Bronze M1870 Gasser Revolver Made for Polar Exploration
recentItems.description:
In 1872, two Austro-Hungarian military officers named Julius Payer and Carl Weyprecht set out on an expedition to find a northeast passage to reach the Orient by traversing across the Arctic Ocean above Russia. The expedition was well-funded, and among their other specialized articles equipment they had several bronze Gasser M1870 revolvers and Werndl rifles. Why bronze? That is a bit unclear; it may have been from concerns about iron becoming brittle at arctic temperatures, or perhaps to get better salt water corrosion resistance.

The expedition was not successful in finding passage to Japan, but it did discover and chart an archipelago which they named Franz Josef Land (now claimed by Russia). Despite losing their ship trapped in ice and having to escape by sledges and longboats, the expedition was able to successfully make it to Novaya Zemlya where they met up with Russian fishermen who helped them get transport back to Norway. It was a two year journey, and only one man died along the way (of tuberculosis). Ultimately, it led to a series of internationally coordinated sets of scientific expeditions (International Polar Years) to study the arctic in 1882/3, 1932/3, 1957/8, and 2007-2009.

Article on the 1872 expedition and its ramifications:

Part 1 - https://www.polarresearch.at/the-discovery-of-franz-josef-land-150-years-ago-and-its-impact-on-international-polar-research/

Part 2 - https://www.polarresearch.at/the-discovery-of-franz-josef-land-150-years-ago-and-its-impact-on-international-polar-research-part-2/

recentItems.title: Drone Chaos & an Epic Pool Party: Finnish Brutality 2026 Day 2
recentItems.description:
See all my kit here:
https://varusteleka.com/en/collections/ian-mccollum-brutality-loadout
Use code FIRETOTHEBALLS26 for 15% off your whole order at Varusteleka!

Today we have stages 6-10 from Finnish Brutality 2026. I ran the match in pseudo contractor type kit, with a Stanzel SAK-21 and a Laugo Remus, with kit from Varusteleka (field shirt, tactical jeans, low-profile plate carrier, and more). The stages really did set a new standard, with a bigger and better water feature and a truly chaotic and immersive trench complex for stage 10. Huge thanks to Varusteleka and everyone who helped make the match possible!
